```http
POST /v1/inbound/ingest/{env}
```

For a mail provider or a server of yours that receives mail and should pass it on over HTTP instead of SMTP. The body is the raw message (RFC 5322). It is signed with the environment's ingest secret (dashboard: Inbound, HTTP ingest): `X-Njiwa-Timestamp` is the Unix time in seconds, within 5 minutes of the server's, and `X-Njiwa-Signature` is `v1=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `&lt;timestamp&gt;.&lt;body&gt;`. Every signature problem is the same `401 invalid_signature`. Envelope recipients come from `X-Njiwa-Recipients` (comma-separated), otherwise from `To` and `Cc`; only enabled inbound addresses of this environment are kept. The message is then parsed, stored, forwarded and reported (`inbound.received`) exactly like mail received over SMTP. Sending the same signed request again returns `duplicate: true` and stores nothing.

## Authentication

None. This endpoint is public: it is called by browsers or mail clients, never with your API key.

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | string (uuid) | yes | The environment id shown with the secret. |
| `X-Njiwa-Timestamp` | header | string | yes | &nbsp; |
| `X-Njiwa-Signature` | header | string | yes | &nbsp; |
| `X-Njiwa-Recipients` | header | string | no | &nbsp; |
| `X-Njiwa-Envelope-From` | header | string | no | &nbsp; |

## Request body

Content type: `message/rfc822`. Required.

A `string (binary)`.

## Code examples

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$NJIWA_MAIL_URL/v1/inbound/ingest/6f1c2d0e-3b52-4d49-9a43-7d1f0c5e8a11" \
  -H "Content-Type: message/rfc822" \
  --data-binary @message.eml
```

## Responses

Already received

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (uuid) | no | &nbsp; |
| `duplicate` | boolean | no | &nbsp; |

## Error codes

Errors share one shape: `error.code` is stable, `error.message` is optional detail. Retry only timeouts, network errors, `429` and `5xx`, with the same idempotency key; fix the request for every other `4xx`.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_signature` | 401 | Inbound ingest: missing, wrong or stale signature, or ingest is not turned on |
| `invalid_message` | 422 | Inbound ingest: the body is not a message and no `X-Njiwa-Recipients` was given |
| `no_inbound_recipient` | 422 | Inbound ingest: none of the recipients is an inbound address of this environment |
| `service_unavailable` | 503 | Storage was unavailable. Nothing was accepted |

Every code is explained on [Rate limits and errors](/docs/api/rate-limits-and-errors).
